title: A Spine Robotic-Assisted Navigation System for Pedicle Screw Placement
protocol: Use sterile surgical drapes to prevent contact with unprepared surfaces.
Wear sterile surgical gowns over scrub suits during surgery.
Remove components that can affect fluoroscopy from the surgical site.
Place the patient in a prone position after administering anesthesia.
Clean and sterilize the surgical site of the patient.
Cover the operative site at the surgical site of the patient.
Place the sterile surgical drape on the patient, except at the surgical site.
Anchor the FF to the patient using one of the two methods according to needs.
Place two percutaneous wires on the posterior iliac crest under fluoroscopy if anchoring to the iliac bone.
Check the entry point for accuracy and mark it with a marker pen.
Insert the first percutaneous pin into the patient’s posterior iliac crest using a power drill (1000 RPM).
Place the FF along with the first percutaneous pin.
Adjust the FF until it is recognized by the optical tracking camera.
Fix the FF to the first percutaneous pin using a screwdriver.
Insert the second percutaneous pin along with a hole on the FF using a power drill (1000 RPM).
Fix the screw on the FF to the second percutaneous pin using screwdriver.
Place a wire (Φ = 1.5 mm) on the patient’s back as a reference under fluoroscopy.
Check the surgical field under fluoroscopy.
Repeat the step if surgeon has concern about the surgical field.
Mark the surgical field by using a marker pen.
Incise the skin tissue on surgical field using a surgical scalpel.
Fix the FF to the spinous process using a screwdriver.
Avoid interfering with the surgical staff.
Avoid blocking the optical tracking camera.
Ensure the tracker is stable and recognized by the optical tracking system.
Sterilize the navigational toolkit and place it on the operating table.
Transfer the patient’s preoperative CT images to the system through DVD or USB.
Crop the image size to adjust the orientation based on surgical needs.
Label each vertebra with the anterior-posterior view and lateral view using the PSNS software labeling interface.
Differentiate the intervertebral disc for subsequent steps to be identified.
Select the optimal screw length and implant dimensions based on the device software.
Plan the optimal positioning and trajectory of the screw based on 3D and multi-planar image reconstruction of the preoperative CT scan.
Confirm that all planned screws are correct and appropriate.
Enter the DRF monitoring interface in PSNS software, which includes multiple planar views and a 3D volume.
Ensure all DRFs are within the vision area of the optical tracking system (range B).
Verify stable recognition by the tracking system when the DRF vector arrow is displayed on the user interface.
Perform subperiosteal dissection bilaterally along the spinous process, laminae out to the tips of the transverse processes at all levels.
Remove facet joint capsules to expose joints.
Use self-retained retractors to hold musculature aside and aid in vertebra exposure.
Select at least four non-coplanar feature points on the patient’s pre-operative 3D reconstruction CT images.
Contact the tip of the probe with the first selected feature point in the surgical area.
Press the probe selection button on the software interface to confirm the access point.
Repeat steps 2.8.1.2-2.8.1.3 until the four feature points selected in step 2.8.1.1 are confirmed.
Press the calculation button on the software interface to calculate the result of the landmark registration.
Confirm that the registration accuracy meets the needs of the clinical indications (<5 mm).
If the result is not satisfactory, repeat steps 2.8.1.1-2.8.1.5 until the registration result meets the acceptance criteria.
Use the probe tip to continuously contact any point on the bone surface in the actual surgical area.
Press the probe selection button on the software interface to confirm the access point.
Move the probe and repeat steps 2.8.2.1-2.8.2.2 until at least 50 pick points are completed.
Press the calculation button on the software interface to calculate the surface matching result.
Confirm that the registration accuracy meets the needs of the clinical indications (<0.5 mm).
If the result is not satisfactory, repeat steps 2.8.2.1-2.8.2.4 until the registration results meet the acceptance criteria.
Use the probe to select obvious anatomical landmarks of the surgical area for confirmation once the registration result is accepted.
Maintain appropriate reflection and reception of infrared light during surgery.
Adjust the camera such that the surgical field is at the center of the camera’s detection range.
Cover the handpiece with sterilization drapes.
Install surgical instruments on the robot, e.g., trocar (Φ = 5 mm) and k-pin (Φ = 1.8 mm).
Turn the angle of the handpiece in space so that the two circles representing the angle coincide on the software interface.
Horizontally and vertically move the position of the handpiece in space to align the dots with the entry points of the planned path.
Activate the drill function of the handpiece.
Drill instruments mounted on the front end into the patient's body along the planned path.
Use the c-arm to confirm the position of k-pin and trocar.
Remove the k-pin and trocar if positions are not correct under fluoroscopy.
Drill into the pedicle again until the k-pin and trocar insert into prone positions under fluoroscopy.
Determine whether the instrument is located in the oval area formed by the pedicle in the perspective image under AP view.
Determine whether the instrument is within the range of the pedicle and vertebra under LAT view.
Replace K-pin and trocar with guidewires (Φ = 1.5 mm, L = 400 mm).
Insert the pedicle screw through the guidewires.
Repeat steps to complete all surgical planning paths.
